# Turingo

> Turingo is a macOS coordinator for Claude Code and Codex. You talk to it by voice or chat, and it runs your projects according to what you agreed: it hands tasks to agent sessions, requires evidence of completion and reports back. Under construction and in testing; waitlist at https://turingo.app/.

## What Turingo does

- Coordinates sessions of Claude Code and Codex across several projects; the agent is chosen separately for the coordinator and for each session.
- Tasks have states; closing a task requires evidence (a result, a file, a test), not only an agent saying "done".
- One owner per session: if you have a session open in Terminal, tasks for it wait until you close it.
- Approvals and questions from agents can be heard and answered by voice; announcement modes: voice, silent, do not disturb.
- Model and effort are set per role; watching sessions does not consume tokens.

## Voice and chat

- Talk with push-to-talk or voice detection, or type in the chat window.
- Speech recognition can run locally on the Mac, or through your own Groq key.
- Voice output: ElevenLabs (your key), the macOS system voice, or a local model.
- A small animated face shows whether Turingo is listening, thinking, waiting for a decision or done. Personality is a bonus, not the main feature.

## Privacy

- No Turingo server. Conversations, memory and settings stay on your Mac.
- You use your own accounts and keys and pay providers directly. Content goes only to the model provider you choose and the voice services you turn on.

## Status

Under construction and in testing. No release date announced. Requires macOS 14 or later. Join the waitlist at https://turingo.app/.

## Who builds it

AI Fresh, a software studio in Wrocław, Poland (https://aifresh.pl/). Working method: https://aifresh.pl/jak-pracujemy/
